title: A rejected role job is never torn down: its worker session and worktree leak
description:
OBSERVED: after epic ncv, three herdr sessions named tick-pxc-* sat idle for hours — one per rejected review attempt (9, 10, 11). The operator spotted them; nothing in ticfac did.

The feed shows the mechanism exactly. Attempts 9, 10 and 11 each go:

    rejected      finding_untriaged: ...
    run_held      ...
    redispatched  attempt N settled with nothing ... a new attempt is dispatched

with NO cleaned_up line. Attempt 12, which passed, has one:

    closed        closed behind a validated review-epic answer
    cleaned_up    attempt 12 of pxc is merged into epic/ncv and the tick is closed

dispatch.go's redispatchAttempt branch (~line 482) records the redispatch, increments the rung and s. It never disposes the spent attempt's worker. Ordinary ticks reach disposeRefused (~367/372); this path does not.

So every rejected role job leaks a worker session, its pane and its worktree. Phase 4 leaked three from one tick, and the leak is proportional to 80x's re-dispatch loop — which re-dispatches a review on byte-identical source until it reports nothing.

Work:
- Dispose the spent attempt before dispatching its successor, by the same path a refused ordinary tick takes (and after kvn: worktree first, then branch).
- Emit cleaned_up so the feed shows it happened; today the absence is the only evidence.
- Test: reject a role job, redispatch, and assert the previous attempt's executor handle is torn down and its worktree gone.

Related: 80x (why there were three, not one), kvn (disposal ordering), qqy (leaked refs).
notes:
2026-09-19 23:57 - Correction: a shell-quoting slip mangled one line of the description. It should read:

  dispatch.go's redispatchAttempt branch (~line 482) records the redispatch,
  increments the rung and "continue"s to the next tick. It never disposes the
  spent attempt's worker.
2026-09-20 11:35 - 2026-09-20 — 80x found this independently while fixing the re-dispatch loop, and its report escalates the defect:

'When closeRoleTick refuses (untriaged findings), processRoleJob returns the refusal without calling disposeRefused, so a refused review attempt leaves a live credential file, a registered worktree and a branch behind — and WITH TICK 80x's FIX THE RESUME NEVER ADOPTS THAT ATTEMPT, so nothing will ever come back for them.'

Two things change:
1. The precise site is named: closeRoleTick's refusal path in processRoleJob, and disposeRefused's own comment says the gate's refusals were meant to be in its set. One branch was missed.
2. The leak is now PERMANENT. Before 80x, a resume re-dispatched the role tick and the stale attempt might eventually be swept; after 80x the resume closes behind the recorded decision instead, so nothing ever returns for the credential, worktree or branch. A live credential left behind forever is the part that matters most — it is a security surface, not just clutter.

That is not an argument against 80x: closing behind the recorded answer is right, and leaking was wrong before too. It means the teardown must land with or before it.

80x deliberately did not make the teardown change, saying it was not what the tick asked for. Correct call — it reported instead.
acceptance_criteria: A rejected role job's worker is disposed before its successor is dispatched, the feed says so, and a test proves no session or worktree survives a redispatch
